summary: nolimit-agent is an obfuscated phishing / bulk-mail attack toolkit
details: Package is published to npm under a benign 'Advanced email sender' description but ships a fully-obfuscated (obfuscator.io RC4 string-array style, `_0x`-prefixed identifiers) toolkit of ~45 files under `.ad/` (from-generator.js, phone-validator.js, sms-providers.js, smtp-health-cache.js, socks-loader.js, web-command.js, x0.js–xz.js) whose documented CLI subcommands are offensive email/SMS operations: gateway-evasion attachment generation (obfuscated HTML redirects, xlink:href SVG evasion), thread-prefix Re/Fwd subject spoofing, DKIM key generation with random selectors, OAuth device-code phishing against Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace victims, mass contact harvesting via Microsoft Graph and IMAP from stolen tokens, MX-direct sending, and an SMS-spam mode. `nolimit web --setup` writes a Chrome MV3 extension to `~/nolimit-ext` with `host_permissions: ['<all_urls>']` and `permissions: ['storage','scripting','alarms']`, a service worker that connects to a local WebSocket bridge at `ws://localhost:9227`, and a Node-side `INJECT_PANEL` handler that pushes an operator-supplied `panelCode` into arbitrary tabs via `chrome.scripting` — an in-browser phishing-panel injector. Package also declares `optionalDependencies` on `@nolimit-agent/{darwin-arm64,darwin-x64,linux-x64,win32-x64}` platform-native sidecars that npm auto-installs at install time; those sidecars are outside this tarball and, per the toolkit's own docs, host a compiled Rust bulk sender. The whole-package obfuscation of an offensive toolkit distributed via a public registry, with a false 'email sender' cover story and auto-installed native sidecars, makes this a supply-chain-abuse artifact rather than legitimate software.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
